title: DHS Title VI FY2026 forecast refused: historical query failed
question: What will FY2026 award-transaction obligations in USD equal in the first registered USAspending query snapshot for the specified DHS Treasury accounts?
resolutionSource: U.S. Department of the Treasury USAspending API
resolutionRule: Use the first official registered-query snapshot under the supplied release policy, reading the FY2026 results[].aggregated_amount with fiscal-year grouping, transaction spending level, the registered award-type codes and Treasury-account components, and factor 1. Preserve the returned USD precision and exclude subsequent revisions. The resolution date could not be verified before the mandatory fetch-failure stop.

reasoning.text: Forecast refused because the mandatory historical query could not be fetched

The target is the exact registered transaction-obligations query, not a DHS agency total. The official endpoint documentation confirms POST, fiscal-year grouping, transaction spending level, and the aggregated_amount response field.

Attempted the registered query for FY2025 using POST https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_over_time/, group=fiscal_year, spending_level=transactions, and time_period=2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30. Included all 22 registered award-type codes and all six Treasury-account component filters, preserving their registered availability years.
The curl response contained no data body and exited with code 35. Exact echoed error: curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer.

No historical numeric print was fetched. The required base rate and six-print reference class therefore cannot be established. No remembered values, broader aggregates, or independent forecasts were substituted.
Prior/update/interval: No prior, adjustment components, sigma, interval half-width, or implied bounds were estimated because the registered historical query failed.

Stopped after the failed historical fetch as instructed. Null estimates and an empty historicalContext explicitly represent refusal; this object does not satisfy forecast normalization. A valid forecast requires successful registered-query history and an officially verified resolution date.
